name: Influenza (Flu)
prec: Rest and stay hydrated. Take paracetamol for fever. Avoid contact with others. Consult a doctor if symptoms persist beyond 3 days.
sevDesc: Influenza is a medium-severity illness that typically resolves in 1–2 weeks with proper rest. It can become serious in elderly people, infants, and those with weakened immune systems.
doctor: Fever above 103°F (39.4°C) that does not reduce
Difficulty breathing or shortness of breath
Symptoms that improve then return with fever and worsening cough
Persistent vomiting or dehydration

name: Common Cold
prec: Drink warm fluids. Take paracetamol. Steam inhalation helps. Vitamin C supplements. Resolves in 7–10 days.
sevDesc: The common cold is a mild viral infection of the upper respiratory tract. It is self-limiting and usually clears up on its own within a week to ten days with rest and hydration.
doctor: Fever above 101°F lasting more than 3 days
Severe headache or sinus pain
Earache or discharge from ears
Symptoms lasting more than 10 days without improvement

name: Dengue Fever
prec: See a doctor immediately for blood platelet tests. Avoid aspirin/NSAIDs. Stay hydrated with ORS. Use mosquito repellent.
sevDesc: Dengue is a high-severity mosquito-borne viral illness. Severe dengue can cause internal bleeding and organ failure, making early medical attention critical.
doctor: Sudden severe headache or pain behind the eyes
Any sign of bleeding (nose, gums, skin bruising)
Persistent vomiting more than 3 times in 24 hours
Rapid drop in platelet count on blood test

name: Malaria
prec: Get a blood smear test urgently. Take prescribed antimalarials. Use mosquito nets and repellent. Complete full treatment course.
sevDesc: Malaria is a life-threatening high-severity disease caused by Plasmodium parasites. Cerebral malaria can cause coma and death if untreated.
doctor: High fever with shivering that comes in cycles
Severe headache, vomiting or jaundice
Confusion, drowsiness or seizures
Any symptoms after travel to a malaria-endemic region

name: Typhoid Fever
prec: Take prescribed antibiotics. Drink only purified water. Eat light digestible food. Maintain strict hygiene. Widal test recommended.
sevDesc: Typhoid is a serious high-severity bacterial infection spread through contaminated food and water. Without treatment, it can lead to intestinal perforation.
doctor: Persistent fever lasting more than 5 days
Rose-coloured spots appearing on the abdomen
Severe abdominal pain or distension
Blood in stools or signs of internal bleeding

name: COVID-19
prec: Isolate immediately. Get RT-PCR tested. Monitor oxygen levels. Stay hydrated. Seek emergency care if O2 falls below 95%.
sevDesc: COVID-19 ranges from mild to severe. High-risk individuals including elderly, diabetics, and immunocompromised patients may develop severe pneumonia requiring hospitalisation.
doctor: Oxygen saturation dropping below 95%
Severe chest pain or persistent pressure in the chest
Difficulty breathing or inability to complete sentences
Bluish tinge on lips or fingertips

name: Pneumonia
prec: Seek immediate medical attention. Chest X-ray required. Take prescribed antibiotics. Rest completely. Hospitalisation may be needed.
sevDesc: Pneumonia is a high-severity infection of the lungs. It can be bacterial, viral, or fungal. Without prompt antibiotic treatment, it can become life-threatening.
doctor: Breathing rate above 30 breaths per minute
Oxygen levels below 94% on pulse oximeter
Confusion or altered mental state
Coughing up rust-coloured or bloody mucus

name: Tuberculosis (TB)
prec: Start DOTS therapy immediately. Complete full 6-month treatment. Isolate initially. Regular sputum tests. Nutritious diet essential.
sevDesc: TB is a highly contagious high-severity bacterial infection primarily affecting the lungs. Drug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) is a growing global concern requiring long specialised treatment.
doctor: Persistent cough lasting more than 3 weeks
Coughing up blood or blood-streaked mucus
Unexplained weight loss of more than 5 kg
Drenching night sweats with evening fever

name: Asthma
prec: Use prescribed inhaler. Identify and avoid triggers. Carry rescue inhaler always. Avoid dusty or polluted environments.
sevDesc: Asthma is a medium-severity chronic airway condition. While manageable with inhalers and lifestyle changes, severe asthma attacks can be life-threatening if not treated immediately.
doctor: Reliever inhaler not working after 10 puffs
Breathing difficulty that prevents speaking in full sentences
Blue or grey tinge on lips or fingernails
Asthma attack lasting more than 15–20 minutes

name: Gastroenteritis
prec: Stay hydrated with ORS. Eat BRAT diet. Avoid dairy and spicy food. See doctor if vomiting persists over 24 hours.
sevDesc: Gastroenteritis is a medium-severity gut inflammation usually caused by viruses or bacteria. It typically resolves in 2–3 days but can cause dangerous dehydration.
doctor: Signs of severe dehydration: sunken eyes, no urination for 8+ hours
Blood or mucus in stools
Vomiting that prevents keeping any fluids down
Fever above 39°C (102°F)

name: Hepatitis
prec: Liver function tests required. Avoid alcohol completely. Antiviral medication for Hep B/C. Regular liver checkups.
sevDesc: Hepatitis is a high-severity inflammation of the liver. Hepatitis B and C can become chronic and lead to liver cirrhosis or liver cancer.
doctor: Yellowing of the eyes and skin (jaundice)
Dark cola-coloured urine or pale chalky stools
Severe fatigue that prevents daily activity
Swelling or severe pain in the upper right abdomen

name: Diabetes
prec: Monitor blood sugar daily. Follow diabetic diet. Exercise regularly. Take prescribed medication. Regular HbA1c checkups.
sevDesc: Diabetes is a medium-severity chronic condition requiring lifelong management. Uncontrolled diabetes leads to kidney failure, blindness, nerve damage, and cardiovascular disease.
doctor: Blood sugar consistently above 300 mg/dL
Signs of diabetic ketoacidosis: fruity breath, rapid breathing, vomiting
Non-healing wounds or ulcers on the feet
Sudden blurring of vision or loss of feeling in feet

name: Hypertension
prec: Monitor BP regularly. Reduce salt intake. Exercise 30 min daily. Avoid smoking. Take prescribed antihypertensives.
sevDesc: Hypertension (high blood pressure) is a medium-severity silent condition that significantly raises the risk of heart attack, stroke, and kidney disease if not managed long-term.
doctor: Blood pressure reading above 180/120 mmHg
Sudden severe headache with vision changes
Chest pain, shortness of breath, or irregular heartbeat
Sudden weakness or numbness in the face, arm, or leg

name: Meningitis
prec: EMERGENCY — Seek immediate care. Antibiotic treatment must start within hours. Life-threatening if untreated.
sevDesc: Meningitis is a high-severity emergency. Bacterial meningitis can cause death within 24 hours and causes permanent disability in survivors.
doctor: Sudden severe headache unlike any experienced before
Stiff neck that prevents touching chin to chest
Rash that does not fade when a glass is pressed against it
Sensitivity to light and sound with high fever

name: Chickenpox
prec: Isolate for 7–10 days. Calamine lotion for itching. Avoid scratching. Take antihistamines. Keep skin clean.
sevDesc: Chickenpox is a low-severity viral illness in healthy children and adults. However it can be severe in newborns, pregnant women, and immunocompromised individuals.
doctor: Blisters spreading to eyes, mouth, or genitals
Signs of bacterial skin infection: increasing redness and pus
Severe headache, stiff neck, or confusion
Blisters in an adult who has never had chickenpox before

name: Migraine
prec: Rest in a dark quiet room. Take prescribed triptans. Cold compress on forehead. Identify and avoid triggers.
sevDesc: Migraine is a medium-severity neurological condition causing intense throbbing headaches, often on one side. Chronic migraines (15+ days per month) significantly impact quality of life.
doctor: Sudden worst headache of your life (thunderclap headache)
Headache with fever, stiff neck, rash, confusion, or vision loss
New severe headache after age 50 or after a head injury
Migraine lasting more than 72 hours continuously

name: UTI
prec: Complete prescribed antibiotic course. Drink 3+ litres of water daily. Avoid caffeine. Urine culture test recommended.
sevDesc: A urinary tract infection is a medium-severity bacterial infection. Simple bladder UTIs respond well to antibiotics, but if infection spreads to the kidneys it becomes serious.
doctor: Fever above 38.5°C with back or flank pain (kidney infection)
Blood visible in the urine
Symptoms not improving after 2 days of antibiotic treatment
Third UTI or more within 12 months (recurrent UTI evaluation needed)

name: Anaemia
prec: Iron-rich diet (spinach, lentils). Iron and folic acid supplements. Complete blood count test. Treat underlying cause.
sevDesc: Anaemia is a medium-severity condition with many possible causes including iron deficiency, vitamin B12 deficiency, and chronic disease. Severe anaemia can cause heart failure.
doctor: Extreme fatigue making it impossible to carry out daily tasks
Rapid or irregular heartbeat while resting
Chest pain, shortness of breath, or fainting spells
Haemoglobin level below 8 g/dL on blood test

name: Arthritis
prec: Physiotherapy and gentle exercise. Anti-inflammatory medication. Hot/cold therapy. Regular rheumatology checkups.
sevDesc: Arthritis is a medium-severity chronic condition causing joint pain and stiffness. Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune disease that can cause systemic damage to organs.
doctor: Joint swelling, warmth, and redness that does not improve
Morning stiffness lasting more than 1 hour daily
Joints becoming visibly deformed or losing range of motion
Systemic symptoms: fatigue, fever, weight loss alongside joint pain

name: Malnutrition
prec: Balanced nutrient-rich diet. Protein and vitamin supplements. Gradual refeeding program. Dietitian consultation.
sevDesc: Malnutrition is a medium-severity condition resulting from inadequate nutrient intake or absorption. Severe malnutrition is life-threatening and requires urgent medical nutrition therapy.
doctor: Significant unintentional weight loss over a short period
Swelling (oedema) in the legs, feet, or abdomen
Child not growing or gaining weight as expected
Extreme weakness, hair loss, and skin changes occurring together

name: Seasonal Allergies
prec: Avoid known allergens. Take antihistamines (cetirizine). Use nasal sprays if needed. Stay indoors during high pollen seasons.
sevDesc: Seasonal allergies are low-severity and non-contagious. They occur when the immune system overreacts to pollen, dust, or animal dander. They are manageable with antihistamines and avoidance.
doctor: Wheezing or difficulty breathing along with allergy symptoms
Symptoms not improving with over-the-counter antihistamines
Severe swelling of the face, lips, or throat (anaphylaxis risk)
Recurring sinus infections triggered by allergies

name: Mouth Ulcers
prec: Use antiseptic mouthwash. Apply topical gels (Bonjela). Eat soft, non-spicy food. Avoid acidic drinks. Ulcers usually heal in 1–2 weeks.
sevDesc: Mouth ulcers are low-severity, small sores that form on the soft tissue inside the mouth. They are usually harmless and heal within 1–2 weeks. Recurrent ulcers may indicate a nutritional deficiency.
doctor: Ulcers larger than 1 cm that do not heal after 3 weeks
Multiple ulcers appearing at the same time repeatedly
Ulcers accompanied by high fever or skin rash
Difficulty swallowing or speaking due to ulcer pain

name: Dehydration
prec: Drink 8–10 glasses of water daily. Have ORS or electrolyte drinks. Avoid caffeine and alcohol. Rest in a cool environment.
sevDesc: Mild dehydration is low-severity and easily treated by drinking fluids. However, severe dehydration can cause kidney failure, seizures, and death, especially in infants and the elderly.
doctor: No urination for more than 8 hours
Sunken eyes, dry mouth, and extreme thirst
Rapid heartbeat or rapid breathing
Confusion, dizziness, or fainting

name: Indigestion
prec: Eat smaller, frequent meals. Avoid fatty and spicy foods. Do not lie down right after eating. Antacids can provide quick relief.
sevDesc: Indigestion is a low-severity, common digestive discomfort. Occasional indigestion is normal, but frequent episodes may indicate GERD, gastritis, or peptic ulcers.
doctor: Heartburn more than twice a week for several weeks
Difficulty or pain when swallowing food
Vomiting blood or passing black tarry stools
Unexplained weight loss alongside digestive symptoms

name: Vitamin Deficiency
prec: Eat a balanced diet rich in fruits and vegetables. Take a multivitamin supplement. Get 15–20 min of sunlight for Vitamin D. Blood test to identify specific deficiency.
sevDesc: Vitamin and mineral deficiencies are low-severity conditions that develop gradually. Severe deficiencies can lead to anaemia, rickets, scurvy, and nerve damage if left untreated.
doctor: Extreme fatigue that does not improve with rest
Numbness or tingling in hands and feet (B12 deficiency)
Bone pain or muscle weakness (Vitamin D deficiency)
Hair falling out in patches or brittle nails

name: Eye Strain
prec: Follow the 20-20-20 rule (every 20 min, look 20 ft away for 20 sec). Reduce screen brightness. Use lubricating eye drops. Ensure proper lighting while reading.
sevDesc: Eye strain is a low-severity condition caused by prolonged screen use, reading, or driving. It is usually temporary and resolves with rest. Persistent cases may indicate an uncorrected vision problem.
doctor: Headaches that persist even after resting from screens
Double or blurred vision that does not clear up
Eye pain or seeing flashes of light or floaters
No improvement after reducing screen time for 1 week

name: Dandruff
prec: Use an anti-dandruff shampoo (ketoconazole or zinc pyrithione). Avoid oily hair products. Manage stress levels. Stay hydrated.
sevDesc: Dandruff is a low-severity chronic scalp condition caused by excess oil, skin cell shedding, or a yeast called Malassezia. It is not contagious and is manageable with medicated shampoos.
doctor: Scalp becoming red, inflamed, or very itchy
Dandruff spreading to eyebrows, nose, or ears
Large greasy yellow flakes with skin irritation
No improvement after 4 weeks of using anti-dandruff shampoo

name: Heat Exhaustion
prec: Move to a cool shaded area immediately. Drink cool water or sports drinks. Apply cold wet cloth to neck and forehead. Rest completely.
sevDesc: Heat exhaustion is a low-to-medium severity condition caused by prolonged exposure to high temperatures. If not treated promptly, it can progress to heat stroke, which is life-threatening.
doctor: Skin becomes hot, dry, and you stop sweating (heat stroke warning)
Body temperature rises above 40°C (104°F)
Confusion, loss of consciousness, or seizures
Symptoms do not improve after 30 minutes of cooling measures

name: Insomnia
prec: Maintain a consistent sleep schedule. Avoid screens 1 hour before bed. Reduce caffeine intake. Practice relaxation techniques.
sevDesc: Insomnia is a low-severity sleep disorder that affects quality of life significantly. Chronic insomnia lasting more than 3 months can increase the risk of depression, anxiety, and cardiovascular disease.
doctor: Unable to sleep despite being exhausted for more than 3 weeks
Sleeplessness causing serious impact on daily work or mood
Sleep problems accompanied by chest pain or breathing difficulty
Dependence on sleeping pills or alcohol to fall asleep
